blocks.title: Final rule
blocks.text: A script that can't fail loudly, can't be run twice, and can't be read by the next person is a production incident waiting for a date.

caption.text: Part 2 of BASH SCRIPT SAFETY. `cd /nonexistent; rm -rf *` — two commands, one deleted working directory, zero error messages. Bash's default is to keep going no matter what, and that default has cost more data than any exploit. This handbook is the full walk from `set -euo pipefail` to a shipping checklist: the eight places `set -e` lies to you, quoting rules that survive filenames with newlines, mktemp and traps that actually clean up, idempotency that makes reruns safe, and a footgun gallery of everything that has bitten the rest of us.
